newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down despite low dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down despite low dlr demand.

text.p: * Central Bank raises offer rate for the dollar
The Philippine peso reversed an early rise to close lower on Wednesday at 26.325 from 26.315 as the market followed the Central Bank's desired range for the dollar, traders said.
"Everyone's just looking at the Central Bank," a dealer said, adding banks had thought the peso would strengthen because of the lack of dollar requirements by oil companies.
Demand for dollars was low, the trader said.

The peso initially traded within the range of 26.313 to 26.311, but it weakened as the Central Bank raised its offer rate for the dollar to 26.34 in stages from 26.32 while holding down its bid at 26.26, traders said.
The Central Bank's action pulled down the peso to a day-low of 26.334 pesos, but banks long on dollars took the opportunity to cut their positions, they said.
The day's average was at 26.324 from 26.325, with volume down to $240.10 million from $308.50 million.
The peso would continue to trade where the Central Bank wants it to be, traders said.
Over the longer term, banks will be watching out for the impact of higher wages on inflation and interest rates, which will affect the peso, traders said.
Also, the earlier-than-expected deregulation of the oil industry may create higher demand for the dollar, they said.
